title: Wendell and the Ghost
premise: Casper Dunmore, a financial-crimes investigator who launders the reputations of the untouchable, receives a calendar invite from her handler Marcus Vane — sent two days after his death. The meeting is a trap set by the syndicate he was secretly building a case against, and walking into it forces Casper to choose between exposing the network that owns her career and protecting Wendell, the ghost analyst Marcus hid inside it for a decade. As the syndicate closes in and her own agency disavows her, Casper discovers Marcus's final case file names her as both asset and liability. In the end she trades the one secret worth killing for — the location of Marcus's ledger — to save Wendell, burns her old identity to do it, and the two of them walk away with nothing but each other and the truth.
about_author: Ines Kavanagh is a former compliance auditor who spent six years tracing money through shell companies before turning to fiction full-time. She writes thrillers about people who know exactly where the bodies are buried because they audited the cemetery.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She scrubs a shipping magnate's fortune until it gleams, hollowed out by work no one will ever credit her for. A late-night call from handler Marcus Vane hints at a case too dangerous to attribute. Emotional beat: competent loneliness, the ache of being invisible in her own life.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Marcus is found dead in an apparent suicide; hours later his calendar sends her a meeting invitation for tomorrow at a dockside office. Her agency orders her to stand down. She goes anyway. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion — Marcus never killed himself, and they both knew it.

chapters.title: Wendell
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, shifting mid-chapter to Wendell's. At the docks she meets Wendell, the off-books analyst Marcus embedded in the syndicate for ten years, who expected Marcus and got her instead. An ambush scatters them. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two people trained never to trust.

chapters.title: What Marcus Kept
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Hiding in a safehouse, Wendell reveals Marcus's decade-long case: the syndicate launders not just money but identities, and Casper's own file sits in its vault. Emotional beat: vertigo — the life she thought was hers may be someone else's construction.

chapters.title: Disavowed
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Her agency brands her rogue; her bank accounts freeze, her flat is searched, and the colleague she trusted delivers the warning that keeps her alive by betraying her location. Emotional beat: duty inverted — the institution she served now hunts her.

chapters.title: Ledger of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Following Marcus's dead-drop trail through Rotterdam and a laundered art auction, Casper and Wendell close on the ledger while the syndicate's fixer, Ilse Brandt, closes on them. Emotional beat: found family forming under fire — trust becoming reflex rather than calculation.

chapters.title: The Price of Names
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Captured briefly by Brandt, Casper learns the syndicate already knows about Wendell and offers her reinstatement in exchange for him. She escapes using a trick from her laundering days. Emotional beat: love against duty made literal — she chooses, out loud, for the first time.

chapters.title: Tomorrow, Again
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. They realize the dockside meeting was scheduled by Marcus before his death as a failsafe: whoever came would inherit the case. Reconstructing his last day, they find the ledger hidden inside the syndicate's own charity foundation. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into resolve — Marcus planned for their survival.

chapters.title: Everything Worth Killing For
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Climax at the foundation gala: Casper publicly trades the ledger's location to Brandt to buy Wendell's life, then springs the real trap — the ledger copy already wired to prosecutors worldwide. Brandt falls; the syndicate unravels live. Emotional beat: sacrifice that costs everything except the thing that matters.

chapters.title: Unattributed
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, coda with Wendell. Case closed, credit scattered among strangers, Casper signs her resignation with a name that isn't quite hers anymore. She and Wendell open a tiny forensic consultancy for victims the system ignores. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — identity rebuilt not from duty, but from who chose to stay.
